fingerprints.story:
The sea was a sheet of hammered pewter under a sky the colour of old bone. For forty years, Elias had watched it from the lantern room of the St. Jude’s Point lighthouse, a solitary sentinel against the grey. His world was one of polished brass, the steady sweep of the light, and the rhythmic groan of the tide. It was a life of predictable, mechanical grace, much like the great clock in the tower that measured his days.
